notes.title: Melee & QoL
notes.notes: [p]Melee was never really the primary way of fighting in Dreadhunter, but step by step we’re finding ways to make it more and more fun. That means tweaking and changing how enemies behave when they get up close and personal. This is just the first iteration—there’s plenty more to come in the future.[/p][p][/p][p]We’ve also made the modding menu nicer to use! You can now stack the same mod multiple times, and we finally squashed that mod ordering issue.[/p][p]-------------------------[/p][p]\[VERSION 0.214] Friendlier Melee[/p][p]* Tweaked enemy reactivity to improve your chances dealing with them by using melee weapons[/p][p]* Inventory slightly reworked for better overview of collected abilities and mods[/p][p]* Item Modding UX flow significantly improved[/p]

notes.title: Nice Things
notes.notes: [p]While we’re busy working on Act 4, we still make time to polish up smaller things here and there—slowly but surely getting the game closer to that shiny 1.0 release quality. It might not look like much in the moment, but if you compare it to how the game was a year or two ago, we hope you’ll see just how far it’s come.[/p][p]Act 4 itself is coming together nicely: the story is finished, most of the environments are ready, and we’re deep into the final boss fight and cutscenes. We also want to add more item sets, enemies, and abilities—those are still on the to-do list, but they’re coming![/p][p][/p][p]-------------------------[/p][p]\[VERSION 0.213] Nice Things[/p][p]If you notice stuttering, try switching Screen Mode in Settings to "Fullscreen Window"[/p][p][/p][p]* Increased knockback on melee weapons - for higher satisfaction[/p][p]* Additional room variability[/p][p]* Additional visuals in tutorial scene[/p][p]* Improved Durcaan boss's flamethrower effect[/p][p]* Fiend melee attack 33% slower[/p][p]* UI - Sleaker inventory slots[/p][p]* UI - Improved Ability and Skill tree node decorations[/p][p]* UI - Added visual feedback for no available Skill/Ability points[/p][p]* Sounds - New upgrade sounds for Skill tree and Ability trees nodes[/p][p]* Sounds - New tutorial popup sound[/p][p]* Sounds - Improved exit mission and enter ship portal sounds[/p][p]* Sounds - Improved modding sound[/p]

notes.title: Impactful Combat
notes.notes: [p]Dreadhunter started as a small indie game made by just two developers. Even though the team hasn’t grown, Early Access feedback made it clear—player expectations are sky-high, and we’ve got to deliver the best experience or die trying.[/p][p]So, we’ve overhauled combat once again, adding new systems and animations to make fighting monsters even more satisfying without compromising on controls or flow. Both ranged and melee weapons now feel punchier and more impactful, making combat feel even more physical than before.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043932/be5159b123768e4eb73c6702e92d7a68610a9a08.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]-------------------------[/p][p]\[VERSION 0.210] Impactful Combat[/p][p]* New hit, stagger, death animations and related systems for enemies[/p][p]* Weapon handling feel improved[/p][p]* New physical impact on enemies [/p][p]* Fix - Durcaan hologram shader[/p][p]* Fix - Damage effect glitching on low enemy health[/p]

notes.title: ARPG Combat Innovation
notes.notes:
ARPGs have always been about combat, heaps of loot and most importantly power fantasy. The last generation of ARPGs was so successful that characters now slice through hundreds of monsters per minute, barely breaking a sweat. This success has given rise to a new trend: slowing the genre down under the banner of creating more meaningful combat...

In early 2020, I created an internal document labeled ARPG Innovation to compile important topics related to the genre. I knew we couldn’t compete with big IPs on the market and believed that, to have even a slight chance of success with our next game, [i]Dreadhunter[/i], we had to bring something new.

Among various key topics (like progression systems), combat design stood out as the absolute core focus. I explored different approaches to combat and realized there’s a limit to how far you can go with the industry standard setup. The main culprits are point-and-click movement and automatic regeneration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043932/9610427b8d1a4329561a62ffbfe8d1113154a7c0.png[/img]

[h2]Movement[/h2]
The first step to improving ARPG combat is simple: add a dash! Since 2020, almost every major ARPG has introduced dash or dodge-roll mechanics, making it hard to imagine the genre without them. The next step is adding WASD or twin-stick movement, elevating mobility to another level. Now the hero is faster, and it’s much harder to put him in danger, but so far, so good for the power fantasy.

[h2]Automatic Regeneration[/h2]
To challenge players, enemies must deal massive damage in a very short time due to automatic health regeneration. However, when the player can move quickly, dodge attacks, and regenerate rapidly, the only way to create a sense of danger is with extreme damage in short timeframe—often resulting in infamous "instakill" bosses.

[h2]Slowing the Game Down[/h2]
One solution is to branch the genre toward soulslike combat. This involves slowing the character down, reducing the number of enemies, and making fights more tactical. It works well if you want to keep automatic regeneration, which is obviously integral part of current ARPG consenzus. On the other hand, the power fantasy takes a significant hit here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043932/d12ce009f5b1d238da6c225e64f8536b7cb8f597.jpg[/img]

[h2]You Don’t Need to Slow the Game Down[/h2]
While trying to innovate combat for Dreadhunter, I found that there is another way to branch off from the usual ARPG combat design, one that allows us to keep the fast gameplay, power fantasy, and meaningful combat all at once.

[olist]
[*][b]Health Recovery Through Action[/b]
Health regenerates only when you’re actively engaged in combat. You can’t simply run and wait for your health to restore. The primary source of healing comes from melee kills, requiring you to engage enemies up close. There are other ways to get health, but all require you to at least go and pick up health drops from the ground. It may seem like a minor thing, but it’s huge.

[*][b]High Mobility[/b]
The character moves quickly and has relatively long dash with a short cooldown, enabling constant motion. The enemy attacks are set up so that if you stop, they will quickly hunt you down. And while you're zooming around, the environment itself is part of the combat too.

[*][b]Dynamic Enemies[/b]
To match the player’s high mobility and evasion, enemies are faster and equipped with special abilities like special long-range attacks, leaps, teleports etc. Some players who’ve seen our gameplay videos say, “The gameplay is too fast.” But it’s not—try it! It is what becomes possible when movement, controls, weapons, and enemies are in sync and precisely set up for fast-paced action.
[/olist]

[h2]The Result[/h2]
The combination of an active combat loop, fast-moving enemies with diverse abilities, and precise design keeps players in a state of flow. This approach not only brings something new to the ARPG genre but also delivers a unique experience.

What do you think?
Matouš Ježek, designer

notes.title: One Year!
notes.notes:
It's been a looong year for us. After a bumpy Early Access release a year ago, it was clear that the game needed much more work to meet the quality standards expected by Steam users. We have been collecting feedback and continuously improving the game, which has already started to reflect in recent reviews.

Here’s a list of what has already been added to [i]Dreadhunter[/i]:

[list]
[*] Combat overhaul
[*] Environments overhaul
[*] Entirely new skill tree
[*] Extended Ability trees 
[*] Modding
[*] Shop and stash
[*] New items
[*] New abilities
[*] New enemies
[*] New bosses
[*] Act 2 story, missions and a new final boss
[*] Improved enemy density
[*] Keybindings
[*] Steam save
[*] Various UI, sounds, animation improvements
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43043932/4893221dea09853a6e94bbdfb6513b3aa2bc3559.jpg[/img]

But we're not done yet! Here’s our midterm plan:
[list]
[*] Act 3 is in full production and will most likely be released in early 2025.
[*] About 30 new items are in development, bringing entirely new sets and gameplay mechanics.
[*] New monsters will be added, we know you’re eager to face new foes.
[*] New nodes for the skill tree and weapon mods are coming.
[*] There's a list of quality of life features we would like to implement somewhere down the road like proper Graphics settins, Multiple saves system
[/list]  

Many thanks to all the players who bought the game and supported our efforts, despite the lengthy discussions about the game’s price on our forum. We truly appreciate that you see the potential of what we’re building, and we're doing everything we can to make sure you enjoy the hunt!

By the way, here on Steam, we share news about features that are already in the game. If you’d like to see what we’re working on behind the scenes, check out our social networks (YouTube, X, Threads, Instagram) for sneak peeks of what’s cooking.

notes.title: Your Requests?
notes.notes:
The most requested [i]core[/i] features, like Shop, Modding, and Keybindings, have been implemented. We are working on several areas simultaneously and are discussing how to prioritize future updates. There’s still a lot to do, but we’d appreciate your input on what you need most in the current state to enhance your hunting experience.

Do you want more missions, monsters, items, abilities, endgame content, or any specific feature or setting options?

We understand the overall answer might be simply [b]YES[/b] , but if you have a particular preference, feel free to let us know!

We regularly read all Steam reviews and adjust development accordingly. We will also carefully read the discussion below.

notes.title: Combat Experience Revamped
notes.notes:
It's a month after the Dreadhunter Early Access release. We were pushing update after update to significantly improve the quality of the game based on the feedback we've received. The modding system, in-game shop, and stash were implemented, melee combat was overhauled, and many minor issues were fixed.

The next significant feedback we received was that the shooting experience and overall weapon handling didn't meet industry standards. We focused on this topic, and the result is a complete visual combat experience revamp.


[h2]Guns[/h2]
Dreadhunter was a responsive game with fluid combat from the very beginning, but now it looks even better and feels better when using various types of weapons.

We added several new camera and physical effects. Every weapon was carefully set up with new gun handling settings. Kinetic guns have a sharp kickback, plasma guns have a softer but still powerful recoil, and the rocket launcher is simply fun to handle. Heavy guns now feel heavier than ever while having that oomph after each shot.


[h2]Melee[/h2]
Melee combat was also improved for the player to feel even more powerful while slashing and smashing through Dreads.


[h2]Dreadhunter[/h2]
The last piece added to the puzzle is effects and sounds when Dreadhunter takes damage or dies. It helped a lot with the feeling of being part of the game's world.


The overall combat experience is now simply more immersive and more badass.

Try it now and let us know!

* Camera shakes on all kinds of explosions and effects updated

Too many items you want to keep? No problem anymore! We've just implemented a Stash feature where you can store items you don't want to sell or carry.

The new stash didn't work properly with our previous Inventory interface. We had to edit it in a way that all item management tabs (inventory, modding, market, stash) no longer change categories directly by simply hovering over them. Now, you'll need to click on each category first. 

It's slower than simply hovering over them and seeing all items immediately, but the change provides more control and reduces unintentional category selections. Additionally, this change allows you to equip items directly in the Modding tab (not possible in the previous version) and makes the new Stash management manageable.

notes.title: After first days of Early Access
notes.notes:
First of all big thanks to everyone who supported us and is already playing the game. Welcome!
We know the game is far from perfect, we are listening, are here and working. 

[h2]Our next steps[/h2]
We are a small team and this Early Access is a great way to sort our development priorities based on your feedback. Our short term plan was to focus on new abilities and more interesting ability trees. But you've clearly spoken that you need the modding system and the shop first.

TL;DR our new short term priorities are:

* Modding system - using mods and credits you've collected for upgrading your weapons and armor pieces
* Shop - for selling items you've collected and getting the ones you need
* Melee fight - already working on improving the overall experience - more animations, better sounds

[h2]Known issues[/h2]
We've received reports that the game crashes from time to time on some machines. We are really sorry and working on fixing the issue. In most cases there is a single crash per several hours of gameplay, if any. If it crashes more often for you, please contact us on support@tricksterarts.com and attach your computer setup it will help us locating and solving the issue.

[b]EDIT:[/b] There is a chance that the game crashes can be avoided by switching to "Fullscreen Window" mode in Video settings. Let us know if it worked for you.

The game doesn't run on Assus ROG Ally at the moment, we bought the device and are trying to resolve the issue.

Thank you!

notes.title: Dreadhunter - Early Access Released!
notes.notes:
Dreadhunter - Early Access Released!

It's finally here! After 3.5 years in development we launched Early Access of Dreadhunter. 

The current version includes the core gameplay systems, the first story act and around 40 items to equip your mech with. It also includes 12 replayable, procedurally generated dungeons with bossfights and various difficulty levels including Hardcore (permadeath) mode for you to hone your Dread hunting skills.

There's still a lot to work on, such as items modding, the other 3 story acts, endgame and, of course, more content like monsters, environments, items and abilities (as well as improvements to existing ones). Despite that, we believe Dreadhunter experience is something unique and already offers a lot of condensed fun!

Let us know what you think in the discussion here or on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?url=https://discord.gg/tricksterarts]Discord[/url], or even better, in Steam reviews.

Let the hunt begin!

notes.title: Dreadhunter - Gameplay Preview
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=1xFx29L_DUU;full][/previewyoutube]

Hi, I’m Matouš Ježek from Trickster Arts and would like to tell you a bit more about our upcoming game Dreadhunter.
As you will see in a nutshell it is quite fast paced action RPG - where you collect items, upgrade your mech and slay vicious monsters. 

[h2]Combat[/h2]
We really focused on fluid combat experience and are working hard to deliver an interesting second by second gameplay.

The monsters are both fast and deadly and they constantly keep the player in motion. This includes fast transition between ranged and melee combat and swift dash for movement. 

We designed the core gameplay loop as smooth as possible and in a really decent tempo. And trust me there’s lots of rapid dashing, slashing and smashing.

[h2]Guns[/h2]
We wanted guns in Dreadhunter to feel special – heavy and empowering. There are three gun sizes to equip your mech with. You can swap them instantly depending on the threat you are facing and  ammo remaining.

At the moment there are three types of guns – kinetic, explosive and plasma. Of course we expect more of them to come. 

There are various melee weapons to choose from too. Because we know there’s something satisfying in smashing a group of aliens with a rocket hammer.

[h2]Monsters[/h2]
Enemies are not only fast and deadly, some of them can reposition themselves during combat and some have special attacks. Monsters wielding a gun can also hit you hard if you’ll get too close to them.

Each enemy attack can be avoided by dash or simply by proper possitioning. And what’s important there are no soldiers with machineguns who would simply spray bullets on you. 

[h2]Environment[/h2]
The levels you see are procedurally generated, you will never play the same map twice. 

We have a special system that allows as having both variety and handcrafted arenas suitable for combat.  We carefully defined combinations of monsters to make each encounter fun to play.

[h2]Items[/h2]
The inventory is not there yet, it is still something to be implemented. But you can already collect items and use them. 

We designed all the item types to meaningfully change the way you play. Like gloves that add extra plasma balls to all your plasma guns or leg gear that adds an extra explosion to your basic dash or thrusters that add more dashes in general. 

By collecting items you can build interesting sets and find item combinations that suit your own playstyle.

[h2]Boss Fights[/h2]
Boss fights also play a big role in Dreadhunter. The main objective of most missions is to find and hunt down a boss. Each story act then results in a boss fight with a massive monster. You might have seen one of them in our reveal trailer.

[h2]Social[/h2]
There’s still a lot to cover (abilities, character and item upgrades), we will talk about them next time. Don’t forget to follow us on our social channels and wishlist Dreadhunter on Steam!
